meta.title: Mehrdad Abedin — Solution Architect · AI & Microsoft Technologies
meta.description: Solution architect with nearly 20 years of experience in software development, IT consulting and Microsoft technologies: AI, Azure, Power Platform, Dynamics 365 and full-stack development.

hero.lead: I turn *complex* technical and business problems into *practical* solutions, built around the people who use them.
hero.intro: Nearly 20 years of experience across software development, IT consulting, Microsoft technologies and solution architecture.

capabilities.title: A catalogue of what I do.
capabilities.intro: Seven areas of work, from architecture down to code. Real projects rarely touch just one of them — the interesting part is where they meet.

ai.title: AI & AI-powered applications
ai.body: Applications that bring in artificial intelligence where it adds real value, from the first idea and proof of concept to a product people can use.

azure.title: Microsoft Azure & Microsoft technologies
azure.body: Solutions on the Microsoft ecosystem with an architect's judgement: which piece to use, how it fits with the rest, and how to keep it healthy over time.

powerPlatform.title: Power Platform
powerPlatform.body: Business apps and automations on Power Platform, connected to the systems the organisation already relies on.

dynamics.title: Microsoft Dynamics 365
dynamics.body: Dynamics 365 solutions shaped around how the business actually works, and integrated with the rest of its systems.

fullstack.title: Full-stack web development
fullstack.body: Complete web applications, from the front end through the back end to the database.

integration.title: APIs, automation & integrations
integration.body: Well-designed APIs, automated processes and integrations that make separate systems behave as one.

data.title: Data, analytics & business applications
data.body: Data models, analytics and business applications that turn information into decisions.

showcase.title: From mathematical model to live product.
showcase.intro: A complete example of how I work: a demanding domain, a rigorous engine and an experience designed for learning.
showcase.tagline: A free poker ICM trainer, built end to end.
showcase.icmBody: ICM (the Independent Chip Model) turns tournament chips into prize money. That is why, in a tournament, a chip you win is not worth the same as a chip you lose.
showcase.description: A full-stack 9-player Texas Hold'em tournament practice system with an ICM coaching engine. You play as Hero against 8 computer opponents, each with a distinct personality. Before every decision you get a baseline-strategy recommendation, and afterwards you review the session with statistics, hand history and ICM-aware feedback.
showcase.authority: The backend is the single source of truth: it owns all authoritative game state.

highlights.title: A real poker engine
highlights.body: Hand evaluator, betting rules and multiway side pots with exact chip conservation.

highlights.title: Tournament engine
highlights.body: Blind structure and timer, just like a real tournament.

highlights.title: 8 AI personalities
highlights.body: Opponents with distinct styles and ranges that depend on position and stack size.

highlights.title: ICM mathematics
highlights.body: Exact ICM equity, bubble pressure, risk premium, an equity engine (exact and Monte Carlo), a 13×13 range matrix and a push/fold engine.

highlights.title: Coaching at your level
highlights.body: Beginner, Intermediate and Advanced coach modes, plus a test mode that grades every decision.

highlights.title: On Android too
highlights.body: The same app, packaged for Android with Capacitor.

security.title: Light security assessment.
security.intro: A focused, manual review of what your application or service exposes, to help you spot weak spots early.
security.promiseBody: Findings are identified and documented, never exploited. No destructive testing, no denial of service, no data extraction, and the work stays within the agreed scope.

steps.title: Scope & authorisation
steps.body: We agree what is in scope and what is not. Nothing starts without written authorisation.

steps.title: Manual review
steps.body: A hands-on look at the exposed surface: configuration, authentication, sessions, access control and more.

steps.title: Documentation
steps.body: Each finding is recorded with what was observed and its potential impact — and never exploited.

steps.title: Report
steps.body: A clear, prioritised report with concrete remediation guidance.

included: Agreed scope and written authorisation before any work starts
Common web weaknesses, identified by observation
security.note: This is a light, manual assessment. It does not replace a full penetration test or a red-team exercise, and it is not a certification or compliance audit.

items.title: Solving the hard part
items.body: I'm drawn to difficult technical problems. I take them apart until they make sense, then look for the simplest solution that works.

items.title: Learning, then applying
items.body: I pick up new technologies and use them when they bring something concrete — not because they're fashionable.

items.title: Practical design
items.body: Solutions built for real use: understandable, maintainable and aligned with the business.

items.title: Close to people
items.body: I work side by side with customers and teams. Good decisions come from understanding the context well.

items.title: Prototypes & proofs of concept
items.body: An early prototype answers questions that no slide deck ever can.

items.title: From idea to software
items.body: The goal is always the same: software that works, and that people actually use.
